bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate at the University of Hong Kong, advised by Prof. Xiaojuan Qi. Previously, I visited Harvard University, working with Yilun Du and Mengyu Wang.
direction: I study spatial intelligence for physical agents: how to build a coherent understanding of the physical world that supports reliable action in unfamiliar environments.
foundation: My work develops the perceptual and predictive foundations for this goal, from recovering and retaining spatial evidence to imagining physically plausible futures that guide actions and support pre-execution consistency checks.
future: I am now interested in extending these foundations toward agent–world model co-evolution, where agents gather informative experience to improve world models, while improved models support long-horizon planning and action evaluation.

inspiration:
A personal inspiration

Joi in Blade Runner 2049 inspires my interest in AI as a presence in everyday life. For me, the research question is how to ground that presence in an understanding of the world, meaningful action, and the ability to learn from experience.

research:
Verifiable 4D World–Action Model for Robust Robot Control

X. Wu*, R. Cai*, Y. Bao, et al.

Under review at ICLR 2027First author

TL;DR. S4NDBOX bridges visual imagination and robot control through explicit 4D prediction of appearance, geometry, and motion. These predictions guide action generation and enable candidate selection through geometric agreement with paired actions before execution, improving robustness over RGB-only control under scene shifts and in zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

+13.3 percentage points in RoboTwin Hard success over RGB-only after clean-only training. Zero-shot Stack Cups transfer from simulation to a Franka Research 3, without real-world task demonstrations or fine-tuning.

ProjectInteractive 4DMethod figureRobot demo (10×)

GaMe: Geometry as Memory for Multi-View Spatial Reasoning

X. Wu, X. Lyu, Y. Yu, et al.

Under review at ICRA 2027First author

A 16-slot geometric working memory combines evidence across views and augments the original visual–language context for spatial question answering.
